perks.name: Loose Change
perks.desc: Applying an elemental debuff to a target increases this weapon's reload speed, aim assist, and movement while aiming down sights for a short duration.

perks.name: To the Pain
perks.desc:
While this weapon is equipped, taking damage increases handling and aim assist until the weapon is stowed.

Taking more damage increases the effect.

perks.name: Thresh
perks.desc: Killing combatants with this weapon generates a small amount of Super energy.

perks.name: Unrelenting
perks.desc: Rapidly defeating targets triggers health regeneration. Guardians and powerful combatants count as more than one kill.

perks.name: Attrition Orbs
perks.desc: Dealing sustained damage creates an Orb of Power.

perks.name: Pugilist
perks.desc:
Final blows with this weapon generate melee energy. 
Dealing melee damage briefly improves this weapon's handling.

perks.name: Heating Up
perks.desc: Final blows with this weapon increase accuracy and stability while improving vertical recoil.

perks.name: Jolting Feedback
perks.desc:
Dealing repeated damage with this weapon inflicts Jolt. 

While amplified, Jolt is applied faster.

perks.name: Target Lock
perks.desc: Damage increases the longer this weapon remains on a target.

perks.name: Frenzy
perks.desc: Being in combat for an extended time increases damage, handling, and reload for this weapon until you are out of combat.

perks.name: Redirection
perks.desc: Damaging rank-and-file combatants increases damage against more powerful ones.

perks.name: Vorpal Weapon
perks.desc: Increased damage against bosses, vehicles, and Guardians with their Super active.

perks.name: Desperate Measures
perks.desc: Weapon final blows grant bonus damage. Melee and grenade final blows grant a larger damage bonus that can stack.

perks.name: Rampage
perks.desc: Kills with this weapon temporarily grant increased damage. Stacks 3x.

perks.name: Dark Ether Reaper
perks.desc:
Final blows with this weapon periodically spawn Dark Ether charges.

Charges can be detonated early with weapons fire or by coming into contact with them. Doing so refills this weapon from reserves.

notes: Inspired by @PodvsEnemies episode 127 from 21 January 2025 (https://open.spotify.com/episode/27QaoJnY0M7c7Ikhz8CbUv?si=397188c406294fcf) with @Saint_Kabr, @ImpetusAlways and @CourtProjects (PvE PvE-MinorSpec PvE-EndGame PvE-God M+KB Controller): First-choice PvE utility pick for general, and end-game underleveled content, for Arc melee build Hunters. Noxious Vetiver is an arc precision frame, so ghe recoil direction stat can be ignored. At base, the stats are decent (if you ignore Shayura's Wrath as the resident stat monster) - 48 Range equates to 18.79m ADS and 13.42m hipfire, 38 Stability, 18 Handling is 0.43s ready, 0.32 ADS and 0.40 stow speed, and 19 Reload speed is a 2.29s reload. first, look to boost Handling with the barrel perk. In the mag perk slot, maybe look for additional reload speed for manual reloads for when you can't proc the origin trait to bypass reload. For Hunter Arc builds, there's a lot of synergy between the Puglist and Jolting Feedback trait perks - building well into arc melees, aspects, fragments and subclass verbs, particularly with the sandbox changes due in Episode: Heretic. The Dark Ether Reaper origin trait is one of the best in the sandbox for PvE - generate a Dark Ether charge for 5s from kills, and then shoot with any weapon (or run into) the charge to proc a Dragonfly-type detonation which also overflows equipped and stowed Dark Ether weapons to ×1.4 (rounded up) base capacity or ×1.8 when enhanced, completely bypassing reload. If you're interested, vetiver is a fragrant extract or essential oil obtained from the root of an Indian grass, so a noxious version would be harmful or destructive. Recommended MW: Handling or Reload Speed, with a Backup Mag mod or, when masterworked, Synergy to create Ionic Traces or, when the artifact mod's around, Stunloader.

pandapaxxy (PvE / M+KB / Controller): "Did we need another arc submachine gun? We just recently got Subjunctive and IKELOS_SMG_v1.0.3 both of which have better 3rd column perks. Jolting Feedback allowing you to inflict Jolt without a reload is great and plays into Loose Change easier than with Voltshot. Precision frame SMGs have not been popular in PvE for quite some time but they are easy to use." Recommended MW: Reload Speed.

pandapaxxy (PvP / M+KB / Controller): "Noxious Vetiver could be an Antiope-D replacement in the energy slot, or a better comparison is Shayura’s Wrath. Noxious Vetiver has two weaknesses compared to Shayura's Wrath. The first is a lower zoom at 14 compared to 15. The other is a lack of perks in the third and fourth columns. Target Lock is fine but isn't Kill Clip. To the Pain is a fantastic sleeper perk not many people are using but it's not Keep Away or Zen Moment. So in not so many words it is not as good as Shayura's Wrath." Recommended MW: Range.
